title: Gene Therapy for Ovarian Cancer: From Bench to Bedside: Overcoming Barriers to Clinical Translation
content: Gene therapy has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for ovarian cancer (OC), with the potential to complement current treatments by targeting mechanisms that sustain residual and treatment-resistant diseases. Recent advances in genome editing, RNA therapeutics, viral and non-viral delivery systems, and engineered immune cell therapies have expanded the investigation landscape. However, despite encouraging preclinical progress, clinical translation remains limited by tumor heterogeneity, incomplete delivery across disseminated lesions, insufficient transgene expression or cellular persistence, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments, modality-specific safety risks, and, particularly, biological challenges posed by peritoneal metastases (PMs), the dominant manifestation of advanced OC. This critical narrative review examines the molecular context, therapeutic platforms, delivery strategies, and clinical barriers relevant to gene therapy for OC. Particular emphasis is placed on PMs, functional target engagement across heterogeneous lesions, integration with established therapies, and biomarker-guided clinical developments. We also consider the translational requirements for genome editing, RNA therapeutics, viral and non-viral delivery systems, and engineered immune cell therapies. Clinical translation will depend on matching patient and target selection to the delivery platform and route while prospectively defining treatment timing, combination strategies, and pharmacodynamic endpoints.
